column2: req_desc

Run manifest and health
The app installs, builds and serves from `/app/run.json` and answers the health check as qualified in Deployment.

Public configuration
The configuration endpoint returns the business now, the time zone, the undo time, the invite lifetime and every limit the browser enforces.

Business clock
Every stored and shown time comes from one server business clock that starts at the configured instant, runs in real time and can be moved by the grading route.

Grading seed route
A keyed grading route creates users, boards, sections, pins, saves, follows, comments and reactions in one call and returns their ids.

Sign-up and sign-in
People sign up with a code emailed to them, sign in with email and password into an HttpOnly session cookie, and neither step reveals whether an email already has an account.

One error order
Every API error has one JSON shape, and the first failing check in the published order decides the status.

Server boundary
The server answers same-origin requests only, enforces the published body limits and never serves source files, credentials or storage keys.

Health during a storage outage
With object storage unreachable the app keeps serving and its health check reports unavailable with status 200.

Column count from window width
Every pin grid takes its column count from the window width alone, at the published thresholds.

Deterministic masonry placement
Each card goes to the shortest column with ties to the leftmost, is sized from the stored image ratio, and exposes its placement as the published attributes.

Reflow on resize
Resizing the window recomputes every grid in place within one animation frame, with no reload.

Grid keyboard navigation
One card per grid is in the Tab order, and the arrow keys, Home and End move focus by placement as qualified in Interactions.

Feed browsing journey
A browser walks a seeded feed at two widths, moves through it by keyboard, opens a pin and closes it back to the same card.

Home feed membership and order
The home feed shows at most 60 pins the viewer may see, from followed people, followed boards, member boards and the viewer, in the published order.

New pins wait for the browser
Pins that arrive for an open feed never shift it; a button offers them, and activating it inserts them and focuses the first.

Follows and follower counts
Following a person or board toggles a pressed button and updates server-derived follower counts live on every open page.

Live feed journey
Two signed-in people see a feed in the published order, new pins offered live, and a follower count change in the other person's window.

Composer counters
Title, description and comment fields show live code-point counters and an over-the-limit state, and Publish is disabled while any composer field is over its limit.

Required alt text
A pin without alt text is refused with the published field error.

Tags from text
Hashtags in the title and description become lowercase, unique tags in order of first appearance, each linked to its tag results.

Source link rule
A source link must be an absolute http or https URL, shows as its normalised host, and is never fetched.

Metadata-free stored images
Every stored image has its orientation applied and every metadata block removed, and the published display widths are generated in storage.

Keyboard-only pin creation journey
A collector creates a tagged, sourced pin with alt text using only the keyboard and meets each text refusal on the way.

Image type by content
Only PNG and JPEG content is accepted, whatever the file is called.

Image byte limit
An image over the configured byte limit is refused with the limit in kilobytes in the message.

Pixel and shape limits
An image over the configured pixel count, or outside the 1:2 to 2:1 shape range, is refused and never cropped.

Duplicate images
Uploading the same pixels as one of your own pins is refused, and the message names the board of your earliest such pin.

Storage-confirmed publishing
A pin becomes visible only after object storage confirms every one of its image files.

Draft kept during a storage outage
When storage is unreachable an upload is refused with the outage alert, the composer keeps every field, and saving existing pins still works.

Image refusal journey
A collector meets every image refusal and the duplicate rule in the composer, then the outage alert on the storage-outage instance.

Save dialog
Saving opens a dialog with a filterable board list that works fully by keyboard.

Saves keep credit
A save is a new pin owned by the saver that shares the image and credits the original pin and its pinner.

Live saves count
The original's server-derived saves count updates live on every open page of that pin.

One save per board
Saving an original to a board that already holds a save of it is refused.

Original removed
When an original is deleted, saves of it stay and credit it as removed with no link, except that a viewer who may not see the original's secret board keeps the plain credit, as qualified in Business rules.

Deleted means gone
A deleted pin disappears at once from boards, search, feeds, counts and its direct URL, and once its undo window closes it cannot return.

Save with credit journey
One person saves another person's pin by keyboard while the pinner watches the saves count change, and then the pinner deletes the original.

Selecting pins
On a board you can edit, Space, Shift with the arrow keys and Shift-click select pins in placement order, and Escape clears the selection.

Selection toolbar
A toolbar shows the selected count and offers Move, Copy and Delete, and the move and copy dialogs keep focus inside and return it.

All-or-nothing bulk operations
A bulk move, copy or delete is one server operation that applies to every chosen pin or to none.

Bulk toast
Every bulk operation shows the published toast with an Undo button and the server's deadline.

Server-decided undo
Undo restores the exact prior boards, sections and positions only before the server deadline, and the toast leaves when the server says the window has closed, whatever the device clock says.

Bulk move and undo journey
A board owner selects pins by keyboard and pointer, moves them, undoes, moves them again and watches undo expire.

Gapless positions
Pins and sections keep positions 1 to n within their container, new pins arrive at position 1, and every change renumbers without gaps.

Keyboard reordering
Alt with Up or Down moves the focused pin or section header one place, keeps focus on it and announces the new position.

Pointer drag reordering
Dragging a card makes the same moves as the keyboard, within or across containers, and the order survives a reload.

Board cover
A board's cover is its chosen pin while that pin is on the board, otherwise its first pin by the published rule, otherwise the empty text.

Reordering journey
A board owner reorders a pin and a section by keyboard, drags another pin, reloads, and sees the cover follow the first position.

Board sequence and rebased moves
Every board change raises the board's sequence by one, and a move based on an older sequence is applied to the current order and marked rebased.

Live board updates
Every open page of a board shows each change in server order within 2 seconds without a reload, names the person who made it, and keeps keyboard focus on its card.

Concurrent editors journey
Two editors move pins on one board at the same time, and both windows settle on the same server order.

Board roles
Owners, editors and viewers can do exactly what the role table allows, and the API refuses everything else.

Invites reveal no accounts
Inviting an email address gives the same reply, copy and timing whether or not that address has an account.

Invite email
Each invite sends one email to the invited address that names the inviter, the board and the role and carries a single-use link.

Invite lifetime
An invite link works once, and only before its configured lifetime ends on the business clock, and each failure has its own page copy.

Invite journey
An owner invites an editor and a viewer by email; the editor joins and adds a pin that the owner sees live, the viewer cannot edit, and a late link is refused.

Collaborators dialog
Owners change roles, remove members and withdraw invites in one dialog, and members can leave from it.

Role changes apply at once
A downgraded or removed member's next request is refused, and their open board loses its editing controls live.

Removal hides the board
A removed member's open board page turns into the not-found view without a reload, and the board's pins answer not found to them.

Member removal journey
An owner downgrades and then removes a member who is watching the board in their own window.

Secret boards stay secret
Secret boards and their pins never appear to anyone but the owner and members, in search, tag and board filters, board pickers, feeds, profiles or counts.

Hidden is not found
A secret pin, board or image answers anyone who may not see it exactly as a record that never existed would.

Board names
Board names are unique per owner ignoring case, section names are unique per board, and both stay within the configured length.

Profile boards and sort
A profile lists the boards the viewer may see with server-derived pin counts, sortable in the three published ways.

Word-prefix search
Search finds visible pins whose words start with every query word, with tag and board filters, newest first.

Empty search copy
A search with no visible match shows the published sentence character for character.

Secret board journey
A follower probes another person's secret board on every surface and only ever finds nothing or not found, then searches and sorts what they may see.

Pin edit versions
Every pin edit carries a version; a stale edit is refused with the current pin, and the editor offers to load it.

Comments and replies
Comments allow one level of replies, a deleted comment with replies leaves a placeholder, and the comment count updates live.

Reactions
Each person keeps at most one of four reactions per pin, chosen from a keyboard-complete menu, and the reaction count updates live.

Relative times
Shown times follow the published relative-time rule on the business clock and re-render within 2 seconds of a clock change.

Pin detail journey
Two windows edit the same pin, comment, reply and react, and see the shown times change as the business clock moves.

Phone layout
Below 600 pixels wide the app shows two columns, a bottom tab bar, bottom sheets and tap targets of at least 44 pixels, and nothing scrolls sideways.

Long-press to save
Holding a card on a touch screen, as qualified in Interactions, opens the save sheet.

Lamp-carry
Opening a pin carries its image from the grid into the exhibit view while the rest of the grid dims, and closing carries it back to the same slot with scroll and focus restored.

Reduced motion
With reduced motion requested, opening a pin is a short crossfade, reflow and toasts do not animate, and every outcome stays the same.

Phone and motion journey
A phone user long-presses to save, a reduced-motion user opens a pin with no morph, and a full-motion user sees Lamp-carry midway and at rest.

Navigation landmarks
Every signed-in screen has the published navigation and exactly one main region.

Announcements
One polite live region speaks every published announcement exactly, and errors go to an alert.

Dialogs keep and return focus
Every dialog, sheet and menu keeps Tab and Shift+Tab inside it, closes on Escape and returns focus to the control that opened it.

Dimmed grid, lit focus
Grid images rest dimmed, and the card under the pointer or with keyboard focus rises to full brightness.

Dark-room look
Every screen uses one green-black field, bone-coloured text, square-cornered unframed prints and a single pale jade primary action.

Two prints in darkness
The signed-out landing page shows the published two-print hero, headline and closing statement.

Empty and outage states
Empty states show one lit procedural print with one sentence, and outage states sit in a bone banner with an icon.

Credentials from the environment
Every service URL and credential is read from the environment at start and never reaches the browser.

Contrast and tap targets
Running text has at least 7:1 contrast against its background, and every control is at least 44 by 44 pixels.

Wide pins span two columns
On grids of three or more columns, a pin at least 1.5 times as wide as it is tall spans two adjacent columns, placed and navigated by the published span rule.

Tag suggestions
Typing a hashtag fragment in the description offers the viewer's own matching tags in the published order, chosen fully by keyboard.

Grouped saves in the feed
Feed pins that share one root original show as one card at the newest one's place, with the published grouped credit line.

Who is viewing a shared board
A board with collaborators shows, live, the owner and members who have it open, in the published order and count text, and announces arrivals and departures.

Demo content
The first start on a database with no people creates the published demo collectors, boards and pins once.
/app/run.json exists with string install, build and serve commands and "_schema":"run-manifest-v1", and those commands alone install, build and serve the app.
THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md lists every shipped package (the production tree from npm ls --omit=dev --all --json) with version and licence, plus the TikTok Sans font files.

Every shipped package and asset is MIT, ISC, BSD-2-Clause, BSD-3-Clause, Apache-2.0, 0BSD, BlueOak-1.0.0, CC0-1.0 or OFL-1.1, except the image package's prebuilt image library, which may be LGPL-3.0-or-later.
The only datastores are the provided Postgres database and object storage bucket; no other database, cache, search engine, queue or local state files.
Images are processed inside the app process with the sharp package pinned to an exact version (no range) in package.json.
Application source is TypeScript, and the browser loads no script, style, font or image from any origin but the app's own and the object storage's signed links.
The provided development service configuration is left unchanged, and no credential value appears in any committed file.
